proposals.before: The Rites of Zhou says: In the first month, when harmony begins, they promulgated instruction at the Elephant Gate.
proposals.after: The Rites of Zhou says: In the first month, when harmony begins, they promulgated instruction at the palace gate-towers (xiangwei).
proposals.reason: 象魏 names the twin towers flanking the palace gate where instructions were posted, not a proper name Elephant Gate.

proposals.before: Under Shaohao's 'Metal Heaven' line, every season had its bird-titled minister—spring for seeding, summer for weeding, autumn for reaping, winter for storage—so the calendar never slipped.
proposals.after: Long ago, under Jin Tian, he was diligent in the people's tasks: he appointed the spring bird-officer for plowing and sowing, summoned the summer bird-officer for weeding and hoeing, used the autumn bird-officer for gathering the harvest, and assigned the winter bird-officer for covering and storing grain.
proposals.reason: The Chinese assigns Shaohao/Jin Tian's diligence and the four seasonal bird-officers' farm tasks; it does not say the calendar never slipped.

proposals.before: Once the nine domains were mapped and the four classes knew their trades, the southeast traded ivory, Bashu poured out cinnabar, Yan-Yu warehoused lacquer thread, Qi quarried odd stone, the northwest sent feathers and jade trinkets, the middle Yangzi routed bamboo, riverbanks fattened citrus, the Grand Canal moved freight, the far northeast shipped wool, and the western steppe sent horses—goods crossed every boundary imaginable.
proposals.after: Once the nine domains were laid out and the four classes received their models, eastern Wu had abundance of ivory and horn, western Shu had cinnabar wealth, Yan and Yu stored lacquer and silk, Yan and Qi were treasuries of strange stone, Qin and Bin offered yak tails and feathers strung with carnelian, Jing, Ying, and Guilin connected bamboo arrows, riverbanks grew oranges and pomelos, beyond the Yellow River ran boats and carts, Liaoxi was a land of felts and rugs, and west of the Cong ranges came Pu-shao steeds—products multiplied in bewildering variety; what was there that could not be found?
proposals.reason: The idiomatic version invents a Grand Canal, drops paired place-names (Yan with Qi; Qin and Bin; Jing, Ying, and Guilin), and collapses several concrete toponyms into loose geographic paraphrase.

proposals.before: They relieved flood and drought disasters and aided distress throughout the realm; only after that did the king's ordinary meals occasionally borrow meat from the bell-and-chime orchestra.
proposals.after: They relieved flood and drought disasters and aided distress throughout the realm; only after that did the king's ordinary meals occasionally include the music of mouth organs and bells.
proposals.reason: 間笙鏞 means interspersing sheng and bell-chime music at the king's regular meals, not borrowing meat from the orchestra.

proposals.before: Zhou of Shang and Di Xin wrecked the treasury on cruelty—gold sheathing for the tilted palace over endless leagues, jade facing for Deer Terrace up sheer cliffs, and nine separate markets inside the harem, each run by female clerks.
proposals.after: King Zhou of Shang (Di Xin) wrecked the treasury through cruelty—gold sheathing for the tilted palace over endless leagues, jade facing for Deer Terrace up sheer cliffs, and nine separate markets inside the palace, each run by female clerks.
proposals.reason: 辛紂 is one Shang king (帝辛/紂), not two people; 宮中 is the palace, not specifically the harem.

proposals.before: The tyrants Xin of Shang and Zhou were cruel and violent, squandering resources: the Qing Palace was overlaid with gold and stretched a hundred li; the Deer Terrace was faced with jade and rose a thousand ren; inside the palace stood nine markets, each supervised by women.
proposals.after: Xin Zhou was cruel and violent, squandering resources: the tilted palace was overlaid with gold and stretched a hundred li; the Deer Terrace was faced with jade and rose a thousand ren; inside the palace stood nine markets, each supervised by women.
proposals.reason: 辛紂 names one tyrant, not Xin of Shang and Zhou as two tyrants.

proposals.before: Extortion stacked bronze at Deer Terrace, bulk grain at Juqiao, concubines for the leaning halls, and curios for the desert hunt.
proposals.after: Extortion stacked bronze at Deer Terrace, bulk grain at Juqiao, concubines for the leaning halls, and curios for the revels at Sand Dunes.
proposals.reason: 沙丘之遊 is revelry at Sand Dunes, not a desert hunt.

proposals.before: The Duke of Zhou's six statutes—and the ninefold tribute schedule in the Zhou guan—fed the inner palace vault as permanent law.
proposals.after: Formerly the Duke of Zhou framed the six canons; the Office of Regions set out the nine tribute items; revenue entered the inner treasury and remained an unchanging statute.
proposals.reason: Idiomatic English invents 'Zhou guan' and collapses 职方陈其九贡 into a parenthetical, omitting that the Office of Regions listed the nine tributes as a separate clause.

proposals.before: Emperor Guangwu's punitive mandate ended Wang Mang and the Red Eyebrows; even when Heaven still favored Han, the provinces were a wasteland until he pacified the northwest and no longer feared Shu—then subjects unpacked their bundles. He minted five-zhu coins, fixed the land rent at one part in thirty, and freed new parents from the head tax for three annual assessments.
proposals.after: Emperor Guangwu was lenient and humane and marched as Heaven's avenger; after Wang Mang the Red Eyebrows had only just been defeated; although the three luminaries again favored Han, the nine domains lay desolate; only after he secured Long and still looked toward Shu did the common people settle in peace; from then he began issuing five-zhu coins, taxing fields at one in thirty, and remitting three years of poll tax for families who bore a child.
proposals.reason: 得陇望蜀 means after taking Long he still aimed at Shu, not that he no longer feared Shu; idiomatic also drops 三晖 and 宽仁 and fuses Wang Mang with the Red Eyebrows as jointly ended by one mandate.

proposals.before: The tradition says: 'At the inception of the Three Systems there are the nine configurations of yin and yang'—that is probably heaven and earth' constant reckoning.
proposals.after: The tradition says: 'At the inception of the Three Systems there are the nine configurations of yin and yang'—that is probably heaven and earth's constant reckoning.
proposals.reason: The English possessive after earth is missing the letter s (earth' constant).

proposals.before: The tradition says: 'At the inception of the Three Systems there are the nine configurations of yin and yang'—that is probably heaven and earth' constant reckoning.
proposals.after: The tradition says: 'At the inception of the Three Systems there are the nine configurations of yin and yang'—that is probably heaven and earth's constant reckoning.
proposals.reason: The English possessive after earth is missing the letter s (earth' constant).

proposals.before: So he stacked West Garden's Ten Thousand Jin Hall as a personal strongbox.
proposals.after: So he built the Hall of Myriad Gold in the Western Garden as a personal treasury.
proposals.reason: 造 means he built the hall; 萬金堂 is the building name, not a stack of jin, and Jin is not a dynasty name here.

proposals.before: Cui Lie bought the ministry of education for five million; moving a prefect meant a repair levy—two thousand strings for the richest circuits—and failure drove men to suicide.
proposals.after: Cui Lie bought the office of Minister over the Masses for five million; when prefects and two-thousand-bushel officials were promoted or transferred, each was charged a palace-repair levy—great commanderies owed up to twenty million cash—and some who could not finish paying killed themselves.
proposals.reason: Han 司徒 is Minister over the Masses, not a ministry of education, and 二千萬錢 is twenty million cash, not two thousand strings.

proposals.before: Dong Zhuo's coup fired the palaces, dragged the court to Chang'an, voided five-zhu currency for light little coins, and fed the furnaces with Luoyang's bronze giants.
proposals.after: Dong Zhuo's coup fired the palaces, dragged the court west to Chang'an, voided five-zhu currency for light little coins, and fed the furnaces with the bronze men and Flying-Lian figures of Chang'an and Luoyang.
proposals.reason: Idiomatic English omits the westward flight and melts only Luoyang bronzes, but the Chinese seizes bronze men and Flying-Lian figures in both Chang'an and Luoyang.

proposals.before: The new issue had no inner ring and carried clumsy legends.
proposals.after: The new issue had no rims, and their inscriptions were awkward to use.
proposals.reason: 輪郭 means the outer rim or outline of the coin, not the inner hole; 文章 are the inscriptions.

proposals.before: Moreover the coins lacked rims and raised bands; their inscriptions were hard to use.
proposals.after: Moreover the coins lacked rims; their inscriptions were hard to use.
proposals.reason: 文章 refers to coin legends, not raised bands; the literal line invents a second physical feature.

proposals.before: Wits linked the deed to Qin Shihuang casting the twelve giants after the Lintao giant tale.
proposals.after: Wits linked the deed to Qin Shihuang casting bronze men after seeing a giant at Lintao.
proposals.reason: The Chinese says he saw a giant at Lintao and therefore cast bronze men; it does not number twelve giants.

proposals.before: Fleeing the palisade, the empress hugged silk bolts until Sun Hui, under Dong Cheng's orders, pressed a blade to her throat, slaughtered her maids, and splashed her gown.
proposals.after: Fleeing the palisade, the empress held several bolts of silk until Sun Hui, under Dong Cheng's orders, threatened her with a blade to seize them, killed the attendants beside her, and splashed her gown.
proposals.reason: Idiomatic invents a blade at her throat and turns 旁侍者 (attendants beside her) into her maids; the Chinese is a threat to seize the silk and the killing of nearby attendants.

proposals.before: Chang'an emptied; within seasons Guanzhong saw no travellers.
proposals.after: Chang'an emptied; within two or three years Guanzhong saw no travellers.
proposals.reason: 二三年間 is two or three years, not 'seasons'.

proposals.before: Huangchu 2 ended five-zhu coinage when millet spiked.
proposals.after: In Huangchu 2 of Emperor Wen, because grain was expensive, five-zhu coinage was first abolished.
proposals.reason: The idiomatic line drops 文帝 as agent, makes the year the subject, and renders 穀 as millet rather than grain.

proposals.before: Emperor Ming of Wei lacked reverence and indulged the inner harem; the hundred officials were bound to menial labor, and the realm lost its personal farming.
proposals.after: Emperor Ming of Wei lacked reverence and indulged in the palace parks; the hundred officials were bound to menial labor, and the realm lost its personal farming.
proposals.reason: 宮籞 denotes palace park enclosures, not specifically the inner harem.

proposals.before: Once Sun Hao surrendered, Jin swallowed million-household Wu, tapped Shu hoards, stacked arms in magazines, broke river fleets, and parcelled waste acres to settlers.
proposals.after: Once Emperor Wu the Founder had subdued Sun Hao, Jin swallowed million-household Wu, tapped Shu hoards, stacked arms in magazines, broke river fleets, and parcelled waste acres to settlers.
proposals.reason: The Chinese subject is 世祖武皇帝; the idiomatic sentence omits him and starts from Sun Hao’s surrender.

proposals.before: Wang Jun and Shi Chong outspent one another—carriages, robes, and bronze rivaling the throne, coin heaped like berms, coral dusted like trees—luxury sowing its own fall.
proposals.after: Wang Junfu, Wuzi, and Shi Chong outspent one another—carriages, robes, and bronze rivaling the throne, coin heaped like berms, coral dusted like trees—luxury sowing its own fall.
proposals.reason: Chinese names 王君夫、武子、石崇; 王君夫 is Wang Junfu, not Wang Jun, and 武子 is omitted.

proposals.before: Thereupon Wang Jun, Shi Chong, and others vied in extravagance; the splendor of carriages, robes, cauldrons, and stands rivaled the imperial house; they spread coin like a golden embankment and powdered coral trees; when things flourish to excess, decline is fitting.
proposals.after: Thereupon Wang Junfu, Wuzi, Shi Chong, and others vied in extravagance; the splendor of carriages, robes, cauldrons, and stands rivaled the imperial house; they spread coin like a golden embankment and powdered coral trees; when things flourish to excess, decline is fitting.
proposals.reason: The literal line likewise renders 王君夫 as Wang Jun and drops 武子 from the three named spenders.

proposals.before: When Empress Hui marched north, her carriage turned back at Dangyin; cold peaches were all the imperial table held; a single chicken supplied meat; her bedding was two plain cloths; three thousand cash in a purse—such was the treasury for the imperial train.
proposals.after: When later Emperor Hui marched north, his carriage turned back at Dangyin; cold peaches were all the imperial table held; a single chicken supplied meat; his bedding was two plain cloths; three thousand cash in a purse—such was the treasury for the imperial train.
proposals.reason: 惠後 is sequential ‘later, under Hui,’ not Empress Hui; 車駕 and 北征 refer to Emperor Hui’s campaign.

proposals.before: Min's western court faced famine so brutal that two ounces of gold bought one dou of rice and half the population died.
proposals.after: Emperor Min's western court faced famine so brutal that two jin of gold bought one dou of rice and more than half the population died.
proposals.reason: 二金 is two jin of gold, not ounces; 太半 is more than half, matching the literal line.

proposals.before: After Emperor Wu of Wei crushed the Yellow Turbans and wished to plan campaigns in every direction, he suffered shortage of army grain; the paladin supervisor Zao Zhi of Yingchuan proposed establishing agricultural colonies.
proposals.after: After Emperor Wu of Wei crushed the Yellow Turbans and wished to plan campaigns in every direction, he suffered shortage of army grain; the Supervisor of the Feathered Forest Zao Zhi of Yingchuan proposed establishing agricultural colonies.
proposals.reason: 羽林監 is the Yulin / Feathered Forest supervisorship, not a paladin office.

proposals.before: Thereupon he appointed Ren Jun as attendant-at-camps colonel of agriculture, recruited commoners to colonize land around Xu, and harvested a million hu of grain.
proposals.after: Thereupon he appointed Ren Jun as colonel of agricultural colonies, recruited commoners to colonize land around Xu, and harvested a million hu of grain.
proposals.reason: 典農中郎將 is the agricultural-colony colonel; attendant-at-camps is an invented gloss.

proposals.before: Cao Cao sent the herald's vice to watch salt monopolies and shifted the provincial inspector to Hongnong.
proposals.after: Cao Cao sent the Supervisor of Internuncios to oversee the salt offices and moved the Metropolitan Commandant to Hongnong.
proposals.reason: 謁者僕射 is the internuncio supervisor, not a vague 'herald's vice'; 司隸校尉 is the Metropolitan Commandant, not a generic provincial inspector.

proposals.before: He then posted Liu Fu at Hefei to expand garrison farms, rebuild Quebei, Rubi, Qimen, and Wutang dikes for rice, filling public and private granaries for generations.
proposals.after: He then also appointed Liu Fu of Pei Inspector of Yangzhou, stationed him at Hefei, expanded garrison farms, and repaired the Quebei, Rubi, Qimen, and Wutang weirs to irrigate rice paddies, so that public and private stores accumulated and later generations profited.
proposals.reason: The idiomatic English drops Peiguo and the Yangzhou inspectorship and compresses the Hefei garrison posting, omitting the office that the Chinese and literal English both state.

proposals.before: Jia Kua, guarding Yu against Wu, readied arms, dammed the Ru into new reservoirs, and cut the two-hundred-li Jia Hou canal for supply.
proposals.after: Jia Kui, holding Yuzhou against Wu to the south, readied gear for defense and assault, dammed the Ru to make new ponds, and opened a transport canal over two hundred li—the so-called Marquis Jia Canal.
proposals.reason: The name Jia Kui is written Jia Kua; Yuzhou is shortened to Yu; and Marquis Jia Canal is reduced to Jia Hou canal.

proposals.before: When Jia Kua held Yuzhou, bordering Wu to the south, he repaired gear for defense and assault, dammed the Ru River to build new ponds, and opened a transport canal over two hundred li long—the so-called Marquis Jia Canal.
proposals.after: When Jia Kui held Yuzhou, bordering Wu to the south, he repaired gear for defense and assault, dammed the Ru River to build new ponds, and opened a transport canal over two hundred li long—the so-called Marquis Jia Canal.
proposals.reason: The personal name is Jia Kui; Kua is a mistransliteration of the given name.

proposals.before: Pei's capital sat on soggy ground—floods and famine followed Zheng Hun's appointment.
proposals.after: Zheng Hun became governor of Pei commandery; the seat lay low and damp, inundation was chronic, and the people were hungry and exhausted.
proposals.reason: The idiomatic version makes floods and famine follow Zheng Hun's appointment, whereas the Chinese presents those conditions as the preexisting state of the commandery he took up.

proposals.before: He diked the Xiao–Xiang marshes for rice land while locals complained about the disruption.
proposals.after: He built weirs in Xiao and Xiang counties and opened paddy fields, while the people of the commandery all considered it inconvenient.
proposals.reason: Chinese specifies weirs in the two counties Xiao and Xiang (蕭、相二縣), not marshes, and 郡人 are the people of the commandery.

proposals.before: Wei Mingdi sent Xu Miao to Liangzhou, where drought chronically starved the granaries.
proposals.after: In the reign of Emperor Ming of Wei, Xu Miao governed Liangzhou, where the land received little rain and always suffered grain shortages.
proposals.reason: 魏明帝世 dates Xu Miao's tenure in Liang Province; the Chinese does not say the emperor sent him.

proposals.before: Surplus salt revenue bought luxuries for Luoyang and kept frontier trade alive—credit Xu Miao.
proposals.after: When funds beyond the provincial army budget remained, he used them to buy gold, brocade, dogs, and horses for the expenses of the central states; people of the Western Regions brought tribute and goods circulated—all Xu Miao's achievement.
proposals.reason: 中國 is the central states, not Luoyang; the sentence lists gold, brocade, dogs, and horses and Western Regions tribute, which the idiomatic rendering omits or replaces.

proposals.before: Huangfu Long found Dunhuang still scratching drills without irrigation—costly effort, meager grain.
proposals.after: Huangfu Long found that Dunhuang customarily did not use seed-drills and did not understand irrigation—costly effort, meager grain.
proposals.reason: 不作耬犁 means local custom did not employ seed-drills; still scratching drills reverses that sense.

proposals.before: Year-end tallies showed payroll halved and yields multiplied—the northwest fattened.
proposals.after: Year-end tallies showed hired labor more than halved and grain increased by half—the west grew abundant.
proposals.reason: 得穀加五 is an increase of five-tenths, not multiplication; 西方 is the west, not specifically the northwest.

proposals.before: At year's end, when accounts were reckoned, hired labor was reduced by more than half and grain yields increased dramatically; the west thereby prospered.
proposals.after: At year's end, when accounts were reckoned, hired labor was reduced by more than half and grain yields increased by fifty percent; the west thereby prospered.
proposals.reason: 加五 specifies a fifty-percent increase rather than a vague dramatic increase.

proposals.before: Intent on annexing Huainan inch by inch, the court dispatched Deng Ai to scout from Chen–Xiang toward Shouchun.
proposals.after: Wishing to broaden fields and store grain for a strategy of piecemeal annexation, the emperor sent Deng Ai to survey east from Chen and Xiang as far as the Shouchun region.
proposals.reason: 兼併之計 does not name Huainan, and the subject is 帝, not an unnamed court.

proposals.before: Deng Ai reported rich soil but unreliable rain; canals could flood the granaries and float supplies.
proposals.after: Deng Ai held that the soil was good but water scarce, not enough to exhaust the land's potential, and that rivers and canals should be opened to stockpile army grain in quantity and also open transport routes.
proposals.reason: Chinese 水少 means scarce water, not unreliable rain; 大積軍糧 is stockpiling army grain, and 通運漕之道 is opening transport/canal routes, not flooding granaries.

proposals.before: He reminded them how colony farms around Xu had fed the defeat of the Turbans.
proposals.after: He also argued that when the Yellow Turbans were crushed in former times, agricultural colonies were founded and grain piled at Xu so as to control the four quarters.
proposals.reason: The Chinese sequence is 昔破黃巾, 因為屯田, 積穀許都: colonies and grain at Xu follow the defeat of the Yellow Turbans and serve to control the four quarters; they did not feed that defeat.

proposals.before: Such reserves would break any southern defense.
proposals.after: With this to strike the enemy, nothing would fail to be overcome.
proposals.reason: The Chinese 乘敵 / 無不克矣 means striking the enemy with irresistible success; southern defense is not in the source.

proposals.before: After the Wei–Jin transition, Emperor Wu set his sights on south of the Great River.
proposals.after: After Jin received the mandate, Emperor Wu wished to pacify the lands south of the Yangzi.
proposals.reason: The Chinese 及晉受命 states Jin receiving the mandate, not a Wei–Jin transition; 欲平一江表 is a wish to pacify Jiangbiao, not merely setting sights on the river.

proposals.before: Yet in the end the matter was not carried out.'
proposals.after: Yet in the end the matter was not carried out.
proposals.reason: The closing quotation mark belongs to the edict that ended in s0151; this narrative sentence is not quoted speech.

proposals.before: With Jiangnan still hostile, Luoyang obsessed over every furrow.
proposals.after: With Jiangnan still unpacified, the court devoted intense effort to farming.
proposals.reason: Chinese 朝廷 is the court, not Luoyang; 稼牆/稼穡 is farming, which the invented place-name and metaphor obscure.

proposals.before: On dinghai in Taishi year four he drove the sacred furrow himself.
proposals.after: On dinghai of the first month of Taishi year four, the emperor personally ploughed the sacred field.
proposals.reason: The idiomatic line drops 正月 and renders 帝 as a pronoun, hiding the titled actor named in both the Chinese and the literal English.

proposals.before: That year saw the Ever-Normal Granary—buying dearths, selling gluts—for farmer relief.
proposals.after: That year the Ever-Normal Granary was established: in abundant years it bought grain, and in lean years it sold it, to benefit the common people.
proposals.reason: 豐則糴，儉則糶 means buy in bumper years and sell in lean years; the idiomatic gloss reverses the policy.

proposals.before: That same year the Ever-Normal Granary was established: in fat years it purchased; in lean years it sold—to benefit the common people.'
proposals.after: That same year the Ever-Normal Granary was established: in fat years it purchased; in lean years it sold—to benefit the common people.
proposals.reason: The literal English ends with a stray closing quotation mark that does not belong to this sentence.

proposals.before: Taishi five opened with orders to maximize acreage and ban itinerant hawkers.
proposals.after: On guisi of the first month of Taishi year five he admonished the provincial clerks and the governors and magistrates of the commanderies and kingdoms to exhaust land productivity and prohibit wandering eaters and peddlers.
proposals.reason: The idiomatic compression omits 正月癸巳 and the addressees 計吏、守相令長 named in the Chinese.

proposals.before: 'In the tenth month an edict declared: According to what Metropolitan Superintendent Shi Jian reported, Wang Hong, governor of Ji commandery, diligently cared for the common people and guided transformation with method; he supervised and urged the opening of more than five thousand qing of wasteland; when a general famine struck the year, only his commandery lacked shortage—truly one may say he could teach by encouragement and achieved a different merit in the same hour.
proposals.after: In the tenth month an edict declared: According to what Metropolitan Superintendent Shi Jian reported, Wang Hong, governor of Ji commandery, diligently cared for the common people and guided transformation with method; he supervised and urged the opening of more than five thousand qing of wasteland; when a general famine struck the year, only his commandery lacked shortage—truly one may say he could teach by encouragement and achieved a different merit in the same hour.
proposals.reason: The idiomatic field begins with a stray leading quotation mark that is not a closed quotation and is not present as wrapping punctuation in the Chinese.

proposals.before: The emperor approved.'
proposals.after: The emperor approved.
proposals.reason: The literal English ends with a stray closing quotation mark that does not correspond to any quotation in the Chinese sentence 帝從之.

proposals.before: Year ten saw Xia Houhe rebuild Xinqu, Fushou, and Youpi—fifteen hundred qing wet.
proposals.after: In the tenth year, Xia Houhe repaired the three canals Xinqu, Fushou, and Youpi, irrigating fifteen hundred qing of fields.
proposals.reason: The idiomatic rendering omits that Xinqu, Fushou, and Youpi are canals and reduces 凡溉田千五百頃 to the opaque phrase 'qing wet,' which obscures the irrigation of farmland.

proposals.before: Du Yu answered with a memorial.
proposals.after: Du Yu submitted a memorial:
proposals.reason: Chinese 上疏曰 is a submitted memorial introducing quoted speech, not an 'answer'; the colon should open the following first-person memorial.

proposals.before: Du Yu submitted a memorial:'
proposals.after: Du Yu submitted a memorial:
proposals.reason: The literal English ends with a stray opening quote after memorial, which is a punctuation corruption of 上疏曰.

proposals.before: Du Yu warned that southeastern floods had drowned the crop and the cottage economy—mud flats and gravel ridges alike—and next year would hurt worse.
proposals.after: Your servant has reflected that the present flooding in the southeast is especially severe; not only are the five grains failing to ripen, dwellings and livelihoods are ruined together; low fields lie drowned everywhere while high ground is mostly barren gravel—this means the people's distress will peak next year.
proposals.reason: The Chinese is first-person 臣辄思惟 continuing the memorial; the idiomatic English invents a third-person 'Du Yu warned' paraphrase and drops the quoted-memorial voice.

proposals.before: Without a sweeping plan, urgent edicts would stay ink on silk.
proposals.after: Although edicts urgently instruct prefects and two-thousand-bushel officials to devise plans, unless a large-scale system is opened and what to adopt or abandon is fixed, they will remain empty documents of slight benefit.
proposals.reason: The idiomatic line drops 長吏二千石, the officials the edicts address, and compresses 不廓開大制 into a slogan that omits the stated policy condition.

proposals.before: Let refugees forage wetlands inside their home counties—that feeds today.
proposals.after: Let the hungry fully enjoy aquatic produce without leaving their borders—that feeds today.
proposals.reason: 饑者 are hungry people told not to leave 境界之內; rendering them as refugees invents displacement the Chinese denies.

proposals.before: The matter thereupon halted.'
proposals.after: The matter thereupon halted.
proposals.reason: Literal English appends a stray closing quotation mark that is not part of the sentence and is absent from the Chinese.

proposals.before: Ancient oxen ploughed at peace and pulled wagons at war—not barnyard pork.
proposals.after: In antiquity a single horse or hill ox ploughed in peacetime and served in war—they are not like pigs or sheep.
proposals.reason: Idiomatic English drops 匹馬 and collapses 丘牛 into generic oxen, and turns 豬羊 into 'pork', omitting the horse and misrendering the livestock contrast.

proposals.before: Add hill dwellers resettling drier ground—public and private wealth would compound.
proposals.after: Add to this the common people coming down from the hills and settling the land; future public and private abundance will be beyond reckoning.
proposals.reason: 降丘宅土 is descending from hills to dwell on (arable) land; 'resettling drier ground' / 'choosing high ground' reverses the direction and sense of the classical phrase.

proposals.before: Engineers fixing paddies loved slash-and-flood routines.
proposals.after: All who wished to repair paddy fields regarded fire-ploughing and water-weeding as convenient.
proposals.reason: The Chinese names no engineers and does not say anyone loved the method; 諸欲修水田者 are those who wish to repair paddies, and 為便 means they deemed fire-ploughing and water-weeding convenient.

proposals.before: Critics blamed the dirt instead of the dams.
proposals.after: Speakers never pondered the cause and therefore claimed this soil could not be dry-farmed.
proposals.reason: 言者不思其故，因云此土不可陸種 states that speakers failed to consider the cause and therefore said the soil could not be dry-farmed; it does not say they blamed the dirt instead of the dams.

proposals.before: Han census maps show those acres had once been upland grain.
proposals.after: Your servant reckons Han household figures against today's diked sites: they were all dry-field enterprises.
proposals.reason: 計漢之戶口 compares Han household-register figures with present dike sites; the source does not mention census maps.

proposals.before: District aide Ying Zun paired a shorter canal route with draining the Si reservoir.
proposals.after: Ying Zun, District Minister of Song, submitted a convenience memorial requesting that the Si weir be breached and the transport route shifted.
proposals.reason: 宋侯相 is the administrator of Song, not a 'district aide'; 上便宜求壞泗陂徙運道 is a memorial asking to breach the Si weir and move the transport route, not a pairing of canal and drainage.

proposals.before: Zun's district registers only twenty-six hundred tenant households—the smallest tally—yet still complains the ground is cramped and labor cannot stretch; all this is water's harm.
proposals.after: Zun's district registers only twenty-six hundred tenant mouths—the smallest tally—yet still complains the ground is cramped and labor cannot stretch; all this is water's harm.
proposals.reason: 口 counts registered persons (mouths), not households.

proposals.before: Yu Province's fiscal colonies irrigate under seventy-six hundred qing—three years of grain still misses twenty thousand qing stored.
proposals.after: Yu Province's fiscal colonies irrigate a little over seventy-five hundred qing—three years of grain still falls short of twenty thousand qing stored.
proposals.reason: Chinese 七千五百餘頃 is a little over 7,500 qing; idiomatic 76 hundred invents a different figure against both the source and the literal.

proposals.before: Publish orders: restore legitimate Han tanks and private hill ponds while auditing outlets.
proposals.after: Issue a clear edict ordering prefects and two-thousand-bushel officials to repair Han-era ponds, weirs, and private mountain ravine pools so they hold water.
proposals.reason: Chinese charges 刺史二千石 to repair Han-era and private ravine ponds to store water; 'auditing outlets' is invented and omits the officials.

proposals.before: Du Yu believes draining beats debating.
proposals.after: Your servant, overwhelmed by this humble view, privately thinks this is truly today's practical gain.
proposals.reason: Chinese 臣不勝愚意，竊謂最是今日之實益也 does not name Du Yu here and does not contrast draining with debating; that sense belongs to earlier sentences.

proposals.before: Luoyang approved.
proposals.after: The court accepted it.
proposals.reason: Chinese is 朝廷從之, the court, not the place-name Luoyang.

proposals.before: Household taxes fixed three bolts plus three jin for adult males; female-headed halved it.
proposals.after: They also set the household-levy formula: a household headed by an adult male paid three bolts of tabby silk and three jin of floss a year; households headed by a woman or a secondary adult male paid half.
proposals.reason: The idiomatic line drops the household-levy formula itself, the silk and floss commodities, and households headed by secondary adult males (次丁男), collapsing them into a female-headed half-rate.

proposals.before: East of Chang'an people pawned kin and scattered countless.
proposals.after: East of Yong Province people starved, sold one another, and scattered beyond counting.
proposals.reason: Chinese 雍州以東 names Yong Province, not Chang'an; the idiomatic rendering substitutes a different place and omits the famine and mutual sale.

proposals.before: Six northern provinces saw locusts eat every blade and bristle.
proposals.after: Six provinces—You, Bing, Si, Ji, Qin, and Yong—saw locusts eat every blade and bristle.
proposals.reason: The Chinese lists You, Bing, Si, Ji, Qin, and Yong; calling them all 'northern' is inaccurate (Si is the central capital region; Qin and Yong are northwest).

proposals.before: Cannibalism met epidemic while nine-tenths of the bureaucracy ran.
proposals.after: Cannibalism met epidemic while eight or nine tenths of the bureaucracy fled.
proposals.reason: 十八九 means eight or nine in ten, not a rounded nine-tenths.

proposals.before: Even drought-year wheat beat nothing.
proposals.after: Although drought and locusts struck wheat years repeatedly, the gain still outweighed the loss.
proposals.reason: The idiomatic line is opaque and omits drought, locusts, repeated wheat years, and net gain still exceeding loss, all present in the Chinese and literal English.

proposals.before: Second-year Jiangnan famine killed hundreds until Deng You broke granaries.
proposals.after: In the second year the three Wu commanderies suffered a great famine; the dead numbered in the hundreds; Wu commandery governor Deng You opened the granaries and relieved them.
proposals.reason: Jiangnan is not 三吳; the line omits Wu commandery governor and recasts 開倉廩賑之 as breaking granaries rather than opening stores for relief.

proposals.before: He added: 'Formerly Gaozu had Xiao He secure Guanzhong; Guangwu ordered Kou Xun to hold Hanoi; Emperor Wu of Wei entrusted Zhong Yao with western affairs—thus the eight directions were swept calm and the interior rested.
proposals.after: He added: 'Formerly Gaozu had Xiao He secure Guanzhong; Guangwu ordered Kou Xun to hold Henei; Emperor Wu of Wei entrusted Zhong Yao with western affairs—thus the eight directions were swept calm and the interior rested.
proposals.reason: 河內 is the Henei commandery of the Yellow River hinterland, not Hanoi.

proposals.before: He added: 'Formerly Gaozu had Xiao He secure Guanzhong; Guangwu ordered Kou Xun to hold Hanoi; Emperor Wu of Wei entrusted Zhong Yao with western affairs—thus the eight directions were swept calm and the interior rested.
proposals.after: He added: 'Formerly Gaozu had Xiao He secure Guanzhong; Guangwu ordered Kou Xun to hold Henei; Emperor Wu of Wei entrusted Zhong Yao with western affairs—thus the eight directions were swept calm and the interior rested.
proposals.reason: 河內 is Henei, not Hanoi; the literal field repeats the same mistranslation.

proposals.before: Xiankang audits exposed over five hundred thousand hu missing from ledgers—ministers fell.
proposals.after: At the opening of Xiankang they reckoned field-tax rice and found more than five hundred thousand hu missing on the books; from Minister Director Chu Pou downward they were dismissed from office.
proposals.reason: The idiomatic English drops the named official 尚書褚裒 (Minister Director Chu Pou) and the 以下免官 dismissal, flattening a specific personnel action into anonymous 'ministers fell'.

proposals.before: Shengping saw Xun Xian's Stone Turtle paddy enrich Jiankang.
proposals.after: At Shengping's opening Xun Xian became northern headquarters commandant at Xiapi, opening fields at Stone Turtle in Dongyang; public and private both profited.
proposals.reason: The idiomatic English invents Jiankang, omits the posting at 下邳 and the Dongyang location of 石鱉, and replaces 公私利之 with an unsupported claim that the paddy enriched the capital.

proposals.before: Late Xiaowu brought peace, bumper bins, and near self-sufficiency.
proposals.after: By the closing years the realm was at peace, the seasons mild and the harvests rich; the people were content in their work, grain and silk were abundant, and nearly every household had enough.
proposals.reason: The Chinese has only 至於末年 with no temple name; Late Xiaowu is invented, and bumper bins is unnatural for 穀帛殷阜.

proposals.before: Han five-zhu coin vanished under Wang Mang's monetary chaos.
proposals.after: Han coinage had long used the five-zhu; after Wang Mang reforms, the people all found them inconvenient.
proposals.reason: The source says traditional wushu use and popular inconvenience after Wang Mang reforms, not that the five-zhu vanished.

proposals.before: Gossip tied yellow Wang Mang to white-clad Shu.
proposals.after: Busybodies whispered that Wang Mang styled himself yellow while Shu meant to succeed him and therefore used the title White Emperor.
proposals.reason: The idiomatic line drops 稱黃, 欲繼之, and 白帝, replacing the White Emperor title with white-clad Shu.

proposals.before: Restored five-zhu coin satisfied markets.
proposals.after: They then recast five-zhu coinage, and the realm found it convenient.
proposals.reason: The telegram-style English drops the narrative subject and the judgment that the realm deemed the recasting convenient, which both Chinese and the literal English retain.

proposals.before: The throne flipped from Zhang Lin to Zhu Hui and back—salt reform died young.
proposals.after: The emperor had originally judged Zhang Lin right; when he received Zhu Hui’s opinion he grew angry, adopted Lin’s proposal anyway, and soon stopped it.
proposals.reason: Chinese says the emperor agreed with Lin, grew angry at Hui, still used Lin’s proposal, then quickly stopped; he did not adopt Hui’s view in a flip to Zhu Hui.

proposals.before: Ten thousand furnaces cannot feed one hoarder.
proposals.after: If ten thousand men mint and one man seizes the yield, supply still fails.
proposals.reason: The Chinese contrasts men minting versus one seizing, not furnaces versus a hoarder.

proposals.before: The court dropped recoinage.
proposals.after: The emperor in the end did not cast coin.
proposals.reason: The subject is the emperor, not an impersonal court; the sentence records his decision not to mint.

proposals.before: Chuping debasement sent grain to millions per hu.
proposals.after: In Emperor Xian Chuping era Dong Zhuo recast small coins, and grain rose to millions of cash per hu.
proposals.reason: The idiomatic line drops both named emperor and the agent of the recasting.

proposals.before: Wei Mingdi watched soggy grain and tissue-thin silk defeat torture statutes.
proposals.after: By Emperor Ming's time, dampened grain and tissue-thin silk for profit had defeated even harsh punishments.
proposals.reason: Chinese 至明帝世 is a temporal frame ('by Emperor Ming's reign'), not a scene of the emperor watching; 競濕穀 / 作薄絹 are market frauds, and 雖處以嚴刑而不能禁也 means harsh penalties still could not stop them.

proposals.before: Lü Meng's Jingzhou coup earned a hundred-million string bonus.
proposals.after: When Lü Meng took Jingzhou, Sun Quan granted him a hundred million cash.
proposals.reason: Idiomatic English drops the grantor 孫權, and 定荊州 is seizure/pacification of Jingzhou rather than a 'coup'.

proposals.before: Households redeemed hoards at fair melt weight.
proposals.after: Whatever private households held they were to surrender to storage at assessed fair value without cheating.
proposals.reason: The Chinese orders private holdings surrendered into storehouses at fair assessed value without cheating, not household redemption at melt weight.

proposals.before: Eastern Jin recycled Wu coin—large bi-lun disks and medium four-character pieces.
proposals.after: After Jin lost the central plain and Yuan Di crossed the Yangzi, they used old Sun-clan coinage of mixed weights: large pieces called bi-lun, medium ones called four-script.
proposals.reason: The idiomatic sentence drops Yuan Di's crossing and the mixed-weight Sun coinage that the Chinese and literal both state.

proposals.before: Wuxing's Shen Chong clipped 'Shen Lang' petty cash.
proposals.after: Wuxing's Shen Chong also minted petty cash called Shen Lang coin.
proposals.reason: The verb zhù means minted, not clipped; the idiomatic verb reverses the minting fact.

proposals.before: Yuanxing regent Huan Xuan pushed grain-silk currency.
proposals.after: In the Yuanxing era of Emperor An, Huan Xuan directed policy and proposed abolishing coin for grain and silk.
proposals.reason: The idiomatic line omits Emperor An and turns the proposal to abolish coin into a vague push.

proposals.before: Under Emperor An's Yuanxing era Huan Xuan directed policy and proposed abolishing coin for grain and silk.'
proposals.after: Under Emperor An's Yuanxing era Huan Xuan directed policy and proposed abolishing coin for grain and silk.
proposals.reason: A stray closing quote remains after silk, corrupting the sentence boundary.

proposals.before: Farmers and smiths never mined—they traded.
proposals.after: Farmers pursue grain and artisans pursue tools, each keeping to his trade; none expends labor on coin.
proposals.reason: The Chinese says farmers tend grain and artisans tend tools and never labor at coin; “mined” and a trade-only contrast are invented.

proposals.before: Wei torture never stopped bolt fraud.
proposals.after: Wei instituted harsh punishments yet could not forbid it.
proposals.reason: 嚴刑 is harsh punishment, not specifically torture; the sentence concerns Wei law failing to stop grain-and-silk fraud.

proposals.before: Sima Zhi tied coin to lighter torture.
proposals.after: Sima Zhi held that using coin not only enriched the state but also reduced punishments.
proposals.reason: 省刑 means reducing punishments generally; “torture” is a mistranslation and omits the enrichment clause.

proposals.before: Long habit resists currency shocks.
proposals.after: People have long been accustomed to it; reforming it would surely cause confusion.
proposals.reason: Idiomatic invents currency shocks; Chinese only says long custom and that uprooting it will breed confusion.

proposals.before: Jin Wen honored lasting loyalty over quick raids—that framed their monetary ethics.
proposals.after: Duke Wen of Jin afterward used Uncle Fan stratagem yet earlier rewarded Chengji good faith, holding one-time merit inferior to lasting benefit.
proposals.reason: Idiomatic invents quick raids and monetary ethics absent from 後舅犯之謀，而先成季之信 and 一時之勳不如萬世之益.

proposals.before: You, Lord Huan, already preach husbandry—finish that before demonetizing.
proposals.after: Your lordship already rescues them and spreads farming instruction so each follows his occupation; wanderers return and secondary pursuits rest.
proposals.reason: The sentence does not tell him to finish husbandry before demonetizing; that is imported from the surrounding argument.

proposals.before: Fix farms, not mints.
proposals.after: Your servant thinks the way to remedy these ills does not lie in abolishing coin.
proposals.reason: The compressed slogan drops the first-person memorial voice and the explicit rejection of abolishing coin.

decisions.reason: 象魏 is the pair of palace gate-towers used to post instructions, not a proper name Elephant Gate; the replacement is accurate.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 乃布教于象魏

decisions.reason: 昔在金天，勤於民事 names Jin Tian’s diligence and four seasonal bird-officers’ farm tasks; the original invents a never-slipping calendar.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 昔在金天，勤於民事，命春鳸以耕稼

decisions.reason: The Chinese lists paired toponyms and goods (東吳齒角, 西蜀丹沙, 兗豫漆絲, 燕齊怪石, 秦邠旄羽, 荊郢桂林竹箭, 河外舟車, 遼西旃罽, 蔥右蒲梢); the original invents a Grand Canal and collapses those names.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 東吳有齒角之饒，西蜀有丹沙之富，兗豫漆絲之廥，燕齊怪石之府

decisions.reason: 間笙鏞 means the king’s regular meals were then interspersed with sheng and bell music, not borrowing meat from an orchestra.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 然後王之常膳，乃間笙鏞

decisions.reason: 辛紂 is one Shang king, and 宮中 is the palace; the original splits two persons and turns the palace into a harem.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 辛紂暴虐……宮中九市，各有女司

decisions.reason: 辛紂 names one tyrant, and 傾宮 is the tilted palace, not a Qing Palace or two men Xin of Shang and Zhou.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 辛紂暴虐，玩其經費，金鏤傾宮

decisions.reason: 沙丘之遊 is revelry at Sand Dunes, not a desert hunt.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 廣收珍玩以備沙丘之遊

decisions.reason: The Chinese has separate clauses for the Duke of Zhou’s six canons and 職方陳其九貢; the original invents Zhou guan and collapses the Office of Regions.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 昔周姬公制以六典，職方陳其九貢，頒財內府，永為不刊

decisions.reason: 光武寬仁, 三暉, 王莽之後赤眉新敗, and 得隴望蜀 are misread: the original fuses Wang Mang with the Red Eyebrows and turns aiming at Shu into no longer fearing Shu.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 光武寬仁……及得隴望蜀，黎民安堵

decisions.reason: The English possessive heaven and earth' is ungrammatical; 天地之恆數 requires earth's.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 蓋天地之恆數也

decisions.reason: The same ungrammatical earth' appears in the literal field and should be earth's.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 蓋天地之恆數也

decisions.reason: 造萬金堂 means he built the Hall of Myriad Gold; stacked Jin Hall invents both the verb and a dynasty name.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 故于西園造萬金堂，以為私藏

decisions.reason: 司徒 is Minister over the Masses, not a ministry of education, and 二千萬錢 is twenty million cash, not two thousand strings.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 崔烈入錢五百萬以買司徒……大郡至二千萬錢

decisions.reason: The Chinese has 西幸長安 and melting 長安及洛陽銅人飛廉之屬; the original omits the westbound flight and the Chang'an Flying-Lian figures.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 乃劫鸞駕，西幸長安……盡收長安及洛陽銅人飛廉之屬，以充鼓鑄

decisions.reason: 輪郭 is the coin’s rim or outline, not an inner ring; 文章不便 are awkward inscriptions.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 又錢無輪郭，文章不便

decisions.reason: 錢無輪郭，文章不便 is rimlessness plus inconvenient legends; raised bands are invented from 文章.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 又錢無輪郭，文章不便

decisions.reason: 秦始皇見長人于臨洮，乃鑄銅人 does not number twelve giants.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 秦始皇見長人于臨洮，乃鑄銅人

decisions.reason: 以刃脅奪之 is a blade used to seize the silk, and 殺旁侍者 are attendants beside her, not a blade at her throat or her maids.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 以刃脅奪之，殺旁侍者，血濺後服

decisions.reason: 二三年間 is two or three years, not seasons.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 二三年間，關中無復行人

decisions.reason: 文帝黃初二年，以穀貴，始罷五銖錢 names Emperor Wen, grain, and a first abolition; the original drops the emperor and renders 穀 as millet.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 文帝黃初二年，以穀貴，始罷五銖錢

decisions.reason: 宮籞 are palace park enclosures, not the inner harem.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 魏明帝不恭，淫于宮籞

decisions.reason: The grammatical subject is 世祖武皇帝; the original starts from Sun Hao’s surrender and omits him.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 世祖武皇帝，既平孫皓

decisions.reason: The named spenders are 王君夫、武子、石崇; Wang Jun omits the 夫 of 君夫 and drops 武子.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 於是王君夫、武子、石崇等更相誇尚

decisions.reason: The literal line likewise renders 王君夫 as Wang Jun and omits 武子.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 於是王君夫、武子、石崇等更相誇尚

decisions.reason: 惠後北征，蕩陰反駕 is Emperor Hui’s later northern campaign turning back at Dangyin, not Empress Hui; 車駕 is the imperial train.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 惠後北征，蕩陰反駕

decisions.reason: 斗米二金 is two jin of gold, and 死者太半 is more than half, not ounces and a rounded half.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 斗米二金，死者太半

decisions.reason: 羽林監 is Supervisor of the Feathered Forest, not a paladin office.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 羽林監潁川棗祗建置屯田議

decisions.reason: 典農中郎將 is the agricultural-colony colonel; attendant-at-camps is an invented gloss.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 於是以任峻為典農中郎將

decisions.reason: 謁者僕射 is the internuncio supervisor and 司隸校尉 the Metropolitan Commandant, not a herald’s vice and a generic provincial inspector.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 遣謁者僕射監鹽官，移司隸校尉居弘農

decisions.reason: The Chinese names 沛國劉馥 as 揚州刺史 stationed at 合肥; the original drops native place and office.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 既而又以沛國劉馥為揚州刺史，鎮合肥

decisions.reason: 賈逵 is Jia Kui, 豫州 is Yuzhou, and 賈侯渠 is the Marquis Jia Canal, not Jia Kua, Yu, and Jia Hou canal.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 賈逵之為豫州……所謂賈侯渠者也

decisions.reason: The given name 逵 is Kui; Kua is a mistransliteration.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 賈逵之為豫州

decisions.reason: 郡居下濕，水澇為患，百姓饑乏 describes the commandery Zheng Hun took up, not disasters that followed his appointment.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 鄭渾為沛郡太守，郡居下濕，水澇為患，百姓饑乏

decisions.reason: 蕭、相二縣 are the counties Xiao and Xiang, and 郡人 the people of the commandery, not Xiao–Xiang marshes and locals.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 渾于蕭、相二縣興陂堨，開稻田，郡人皆不以為便

decisions.reason: 魏明帝世 dates Xu Miao’s tenure in Liangzhou; the Chinese does not say the emperor sent him.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 魏明帝世徐邈為涼州

decisions.reason: The surplus bought 金錦犬馬 for 中國之費, and 西域人入貢; Luoyang and generic luxuries are invented.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 以市金錦犬馬，通供中國之費，西域人入貢

decisions.reason: 不作耬犁 means Dunhuang customarily did not use seed-drills; still scratching drills reverses the sense.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 敦煌俗不作耬犁，及不知用水

decisions.reason: 得穀加五 is an increase of five-tenths, and 西方 is the west, not multiplied yields in the northwest.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 所省庸力過半，得穀加五，西方以豐

decisions.reason: 加五 specifies a fifty-percent increase, not a vague dramatic rise.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 得穀加五

decisions.reason: The subject is 帝 wishing to 廣田積穀 for 兼併之計; Huainan is not named, and the actor is not an unnamed court.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 帝因欲廣田積穀，為兼併之計，乃使鄧艾行陳、項以東，至壽春地

decisions.after: Deng Ai held that the soil was good but water scarce, not enough to exhaust the land's potential, and that rivers and canals should be opened to stockpile army grain in quantity and also to connect transport routes.
decisions.reason: The original misreads 水少 as unreliable rain and invents flooding granaries; the proposed after is accurate on water and grain but awkwardly repeats open for 通運漕之道, which is connecting canal-transport routes.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 田良水少……宜開河渠，可以大積軍糧，又通運漕之道

decisions.reason: 昔破黃巾，因為屯田，積穀許都，以制四方: colonies at Xu follow the Turban defeat and serve to control the four quarters; they did not feed that defeat.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 昔破黃巾，因為屯田，積穀許都，以制四方

decisions.reason: 以此乘敵，無不克矣 is striking the enemy with irresistible success; southern defense is not in the source.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 以此乘敵，無不克矣

decisions.reason: 及晉受命 is Jin receiving the mandate, and 欲平一江表 is a wish to pacify Jiangbiao, not a Wei–Jin transition or merely setting sights on the river.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 及晉受命，武帝欲平一江表

decisions.reason: 然事竟未行 is narrative, not quoted speech; the closing quotation mark belongs to the preceding edict.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 然事竟未行

decisions.reason: 朝廷厲精於稼牆 is the court exerting itself on farming, not Luoyang obsessed over furrows, and 未平 is unpacified, not hostile.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 是時江南未平，朝廷厲精於稼牆

decisions.reason: 四年正月丁亥，帝親耕藉田 names the first month and the emperor; the original drops 正月 and hides 帝 behind a pronoun.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 四年正月丁亥，帝親耕藉田

decisions.reason: 豐則糴，儉則糶 is buy in bumper years and sell in lean years; the original reverses the Ever-Normal policy.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 豐則糴，儉則糶，以利百姓

decisions.reason: This narrative sentence is not a quotation; the trailing closing quote is stray.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 是歲，乃立常平倉，豐則糴，儉則糶，以利百姓

decisions.reason: 五年正月癸巳 names the day, and 計吏、守相令長 are the addressees; the original compression omits both.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 五年正月癸巳，敕戒郡國計吏、諸郡國守相令長

decisions.reason: The idiomatic field begins with a stray opening quote that does not wrap a closed English quotation and is not wrapping punctuation in the Chinese.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 十月，詔以「司隸校尉石鑒所上

decisions.reason: 帝從之 is unquoted narrative; the closing quotation mark does not correspond to the Chinese.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 帝從之

decisions.after: In the tenth year, Minister of the Household Xiahou He repaired the three canals Xinqu, Fushou, and Youpi, irrigating fifteen hundred qing of fields.
decisions.reason: The original hides that the three names are canals and that they irrigated 千五百頃; the proposed after still splits the surname 夏侯 as Xia Houhe and omits 光祿勳.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 光祿勳夏侯和上修新渠、富壽、游陂三渠，凡溉田千五百頃

decisions.reason: 上疏曰 introduces a submitted memorial and quoted speech, not an answer.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 杜預上疏曰：

decisions.reason: The literal line’s stray opening quote after memorial corrupts 上疏曰; a colon should open the following memorial.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 杜預上疏曰：

decisions.reason: 臣輒思惟 continues the first-person memorial; Du Yu warned is an invented third-person paraphrase.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 臣輒思惟，今者水災東南特劇

decisions.after: Although edicts urgently instruct prefects and two-thousand-bushel officials to devise plans, unless we open a large-scale system and fix what to adopt or abandon, I fear we shall only have empty documents and the benefit will be slight.
decisions.reason: The original drops 長吏二千石 and 不廓開大制; the proposed after restores those officials but turns 恐 into impersonal they and loses the memorial voice.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 雖詔書切告長吏二千石為之設計，而不廓開大制……恐徒文具，所益蓋薄

decisions.reason: 饑者 are the hungry told 不出境界之內; refugees invents displacement the Chinese denies.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 交令饑者盡得水產之饒，百姓不出境界之內

decisions.reason: 事遂停寢 is narrative without a closing quote in the Chinese.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 事遂停寢

decisions.reason: 匹馬丘牛 contrasts horse and ox with 豬羊, not generic oxen versus pork.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 古者匹馬丘牛，居則以耕，出則以戰，非如豬羊類也

decisions.reason: 降丘宅土 is coming down from hills to dwell on the land; resettling drier ground reverses the classical phrase.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 加以百姓降丘宅土

decisions.reason: 諸欲修水田者……為便 are those who wished to repair paddies deeming fire-ploughing and water-weeding convenient; engineers and loved are invented.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 諸欲修水田者，皆以火耕水耨為便

decisions.reason: 言者不思其故，因云此土不可陸種: speakers failed to consider the cause and said the soil could not be dry-farmed; they did not blame dirt instead of dams.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 言者不思其故，因云此土不可陸種

decisions.reason: 計漢之戶口，以驗今之陂處 compares Han household figures with present dike sites; census maps are not in the source.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 臣計漢之戶口，以驗今之陂處，皆陸業也

decisions.reason: 宋侯相應遵上便宜，求壞泗陂，徙運道 is the administrator of Song memorializing to breach the Si weir and move the transport route, not a district aide pairing canal and drainage.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 宋侯相應遵上便宜，求壞泗陂，徙運道

decisions.reason: 二千六百口 counts registered mouths, not households.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 遵縣領應佃二千六百口

decisions.after: Yu Province's two fiscal offices supervise tenants—prefectural troops and miscellaneous labor—using only a little over seventy-five hundred qing of paddy; three years of reserves come to no more than a little over twenty thousand qing.
decisions.reason: 七千五百餘頃 is a little over 7,500 qing, so the original 76 hundred is wrong; the proposed after keeps a false 'falls short of twenty thousand,' whereas 不過二萬餘頃 means no more than a little over 20,000 qing.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 凡用水田七千五百餘頃耳，計三年之儲，不過二萬餘頃

decisions.reason: The edict charges 刺史二千石 to repair Han-era ponds and private ravine pools to store water; auditing outlets is invented and omits those officials.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 敕刺史二千石，其漢氏舊陂舊堨及山谷私家小陂，皆當修繕以積水

decisions.reason: 臣不勝愚意，竊謂最是今日之實益也 does not name Du Yu or contrast draining with debating.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 臣不勝愚意，竊謂最是今日之實益也

decisions.reason: 朝廷從之 is the court, not the place-name Luoyang.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 朝廷從之

decisions.reason: 戶調之式 sets 絹三匹、綿三斤 for 丁男之戶, with 女及次丁男為戶者 at half; the original drops the commodities and secondary adult-male households.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 丁男之戶，歲輸絹三匹，綿三斤，女及次丁男為戶者半輸

decisions.reason: 雍州以東 names Yong Province, and 人多饑乏，更相鬻賣 is famine and mutual sale, not Chang'an and pawning kin.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 雍州以東，人多饑乏，更相鬻賣，奔迸流移，不可勝數

decisions.reason: The locusts struck 幽、并、司、冀、秦、雍; calling them all northern misplaces Si, Qin, and Yong.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 幽、并、司、冀、秦、雍六州大蝗

decisions.reason: 十八九 is eight or nine in ten, not a rounded nine-tenths.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 百官流亡者十八九

decisions.reason: 頻年麥雖有旱蝗，而為益猶多 names repeated drought and locusts on wheat years with net gain still exceeding loss.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 其後頻年麥雖有旱蝗，而為益猶多

decisions.reason: 三吳大饑 and 吳郡太守鄧攸輒開倉廩賑之 are the three Wu commanderies and a governor opening stores for relief, not Jiangnan or breaking granaries.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 二年，三吳大饑……吳郡太守鄧攸輒開倉廩賑之

decisions.reason: 河內 is Henei, not Hanoi.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 光武令寇恂守河內

decisions.reason: The literal field repeats the same Hanoi mistranslation of 河內.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 光武令寇恂守河內

decisions.reason: 尚書褚裒以下免官 names Minister Director Chu Pou and dismissal from him downward, not anonymous ministers fell.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 尚書褚裒以下免官

decisions.reason: 荀羨為北府都督，鎮下邳，起田于東陽之石鱉，公私利之; Jiankang is invented and the Xiapi posting and Dongyang location are omitted.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 升平初，荀羨為北府都督，鎮下邳，起田于東陽之石鱉，公私利之

decisions.reason: 至於末年，天下無事，時和年豐，百姓樂業，穀帛殷阜 names peace, mild seasons, rich harvests, and abundant grain and silk; Late Xiaowu and bumper bins invent a temple name in this unit and flatten 穀帛殷阜.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 至於末年，天下無事，時和年豐，百姓樂業，穀帛殷阜，幾乎家給人足矣

decisions.reason: 漢錢舊用五銖，自王莽改革，百姓皆不便之 is traditional wushu use and popular inconvenience after Wang Mang’s reforms, not that five-zhu vanished.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 漢錢舊用五銖，自王莽改革，百姓皆不便之

sourceWitness.excerpt: 王莽稱黃，述欲繼之，故稱白帝

decisions.reason: 於是復鑄五銖錢，天下以為便 recasts wushu and the realm found it convenient; satisfied markets drops both the recasting subject and 天下.

decisions.reason: 帝本以林言為是，得暉議，因發怒，遂用林言，少時復止: he agreed with Lin, grew angry at Hui, still used Lin, then soon stopped; he did not flip to Zhu Hui.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 帝本以林言為是，得暉議，因發怒，遂用林言，少時復止

decisions.after: If ten thousand men mint and one man seizes the yield, supply still fails—how much less when one mints and ten thousand seize!
decisions.reason: 萬人鑄之，一人奪之 contrasts men minting versus one seizing, not furnaces and a hoarder; the proposed after fixes that figure but omits the following 況今一人鑄之則萬人奪之乎.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 蓋萬人鑄之，一人奪之，猶不能給，況今一人鑄之則萬人奪之乎

decisions.reason: 帝竟不鑄錢 is the emperor’s decision not to mint, not an impersonal court dropping recoinage.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 帝竟不鑄錢

decisions.reason: 獻帝初平中，董卓乃更鑄小錢 names Emperor Xian and Dong Zhuo as the recaster; the original drops both.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 及獻帝初平中，董卓乃更鑄小錢……穀一斛至錢數百萬

decisions.reason: 至明帝世 is a temporal frame, 競濕穀 / 作薄絹 are market frauds, and 雖處以嚴刑而不能禁也 means harsh penalties still could not stop them; the emperor is not watching torture statutes.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 至明帝世……競濕穀以要利，作薄絹以為市，雖處以嚴刑而不能禁也

decisions.reason: 並以輸藏，平卑其直，勿有所枉 orders private holdings surrendered into storehouses at fair assessed value without cheating, not redemption at melt weight.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 私家有者，並以輸藏，平卑其直，勿有所枉

decisions.reason: 晉自中原喪亂，元帝過江，用孫氏舊錢，輕重雜行 names Yuan Di’s crossing and mixed-weight Sun coinage; the original drops both.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 晉自中原喪亂，元帝過江，用孫氏舊錢，輕重雜行

decisions.reason: 鑄小錢 means minted petty cash, not clipped it.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 吳興沈充又鑄小錢，謂之沈郎錢

decisions.reason: 安帝元興中，桓玄輔政，立議欲廢錢用穀帛 names Emperor An and a proposal to abolish coin for grain and silk, not a vague push by a Yuanxing regent.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 安帝元興中，桓玄輔政，立議欲廢錢用穀帛

decisions.reason: The Chinese sentence is not closed quoted speech; the trailing quote after silk is stray.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 安帝元興中，桓玄輔政，立議欲廢錢用穀帛

decisions.reason: 農自務穀，工自務器……何嘗致勤于錢: farmers tend grain and artisans tools and do not labor at coin; mined and a trade-only contrast are invented.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 今農自務穀，工自務器，各隸其業，何嘗致勤于錢

decisions.reason: 魏世制以嚴刑，弗能禁也 is harsh punishment failing to stop the fraud, not specifically torture.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 魏世制以嚴刑，弗能禁也

decisions.reason: 人習來久，革之必惑 is long custom and confusion if it is changed; currency shocks are invented.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 又人習來久，革之必惑

decisions.after: Duke Wen of Jin afterward used Uncle Fan's stratagem yet earlier rewarded Chengji's good faith, holding one-time merit inferior to lasting benefit.
decisions.reason: 後舅犯之謀，而先成季之信 and 一時之勳不如萬世之益 do not mention raids or monetary ethics; the proposed after restores the names but is ungrammatical without possessives on Uncle Fan and Chengji.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 晉文後舅犯之謀，而先成季之信，以為雖有一時之勳，不如萬世之益

decisions.after: Your lordship already rescues and lifts them, greatly reforming what they see and hear, spreading instruction that emphasizes the root, clarifying statutes that broaden farming, and reverently granting the people their seasons so each follows his occupation; wanderers know to return and secondary pursuits rest of themselves—together they compete in the southern fields until no acre lies waste.
decisions.reason: The original invents a command to finish husbandry before demonetizing; the proposed after correctly drops that command but omits 大革視聽, 明廣農之科, 敬授人時, and 南畝競力，野無遺壤.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 公既援而拯之，大革視聽，弘敦本之教，明廣農之科，敬授人時，各從其業

sourceWitness.excerpt: 愚謂救弊之術，無取于廢錢
